issues.description: generate-stories requires an existing stories manifest for topics, so the documented clean-generation path fails on a fresh checkout.
Default extraction/demo expects story files, but the checked-out data/stories directory is empty.
Ignored generated directories are nevertheless present in the repo, indicating build/output artifacts were committed.
Generated model outputs, including large binary vector artifacts referenced by this manifest, are checked into the source tree.
Generated packaging metadata is checked in, which can go stale and conflict with editable/package builds.
External story-generation HTTP requests have no timeout, retry, or structured error handling, so runs can hang indefinitely or fail opaquely.
Generated stories are accepted with only delimiter-count validation and no checks for banned emotion words, empty content, or minimum quality.
emotion_vectors silently produces NaNs when any configured emotion has zero stories instead of raising a clear data error.
pca_components divides by total variance without handling zero-variance input or invalid variance targets.
The model wrapper assumes a Gemma-like hf.model.layers layout despite accepting arbitrary model_name values.
all_token_activations stacks every hidden state for each batch on CPU, creating avoidable large memory spikes.
load_vectors trusts stale artifacts without validating that manifest model, dimensions, emotions, or scale match the current run.
Configuration values are cast but not validated, allowing invalid batch sizes, layer fractions, PCA targets, and counts to fail later.
Steered-emotion selection does not guard against n_steered_emotions exceeding the available emotions, which can duplicate selections.
Emotion names are used directly in output filenames, so unusual config values can create unsafe or invalid paths.
requirements.txt mixes runtime and test dependencies while pyproject.toml keeps pytest as a dev extra, creating inconsistent install surfaces.
